titlePlain: A VNet and a VPC are

steps.label: Neither cloud knows the other exists
steps.sub: a VNet and a VPC are both private networks with no built-in bridge

steps.label: Two real mechanisms to build one
steps.sub: a gateway-to-gateway VPN, or a colocation meet-point

steps.label: Same tradeoff as hybrid connectivity
steps.sub: cost and lead time vs. throughput and predictability

code:
# Azure side: represent the AWS VPN endpoint, then connect
az network local-gateway create \
  --resource-group hub-rg \
  --name aws-vpc-gateway \
  --gateway-ip-address 52.14.88.201 \
  --local-address-prefixes 10.50.0.0/16

az network vpn-connection create \
  --resource-group hub-rg \
  --name azure-to-aws \
  --vnet-gateway1 azure-vpn-gw \
  --local-gateway2 aws-vpc-gateway \
  --shared-key "<pre-shared-key>" \
  --enable-bgp true
caption: A matching AWS customer gateway + VPN connection points back at Azure's public IP; BGP keeps routes current on both sides.

steps.label: ExpressRoute circuit lands at a peering location
steps.sub: a connectivity-provider facility, same as hybrid on-prem

steps.label: Direct Connect lands at the same facility
steps.sub: both circuits terminate in one shared meet-point

steps.label: A cross-connect joins them
steps.sub: traffic never touches the public internet, end to end

subtitle: Once the path exists, services still need to find each other by name, not by hardcoded IP.
